name: Billy Cobham
hook: A jazz-fusion drummer whose slow 1974 track 'Heather' became one of the most-loved loops in 90s rap.
blurb: Billy Cobham was born in Panama in 1944 and grew up in New York. He became famous as the drummer in the Mahavishnu Orchestra, a band that mixed jazz and loud rock, and then made his own albums. One of them, Crosswinds (1974), has a slow, drifting song called 'Heather'. Nineteen years later the Oakland producer A-Plus sped it up and turned it into '93 'til Infinity' for Souls of Mischief. Cobham is on the map as a sampled source rather than for his own lineage: he was the first of the much-sampled artists agreed in Q21, where each use of his records is a sample connection. His place in jazz-rock fusion belongs to the jazz roots lane, which so far holds only the jazz records later music can be traced back to.
